question.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(4,3,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=-3\,i+z\,j+8\sqrt{x}\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i-j.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j+[-i-j] \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j-i-j \\  & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}+1)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(4,3,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(4,3,-1) & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{4}}+1)j \\  & =-2\,i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
